sections.html:
Kerrville sits on the Guadalupe River and bills itself as the capital of the Texas Hill Country. The parks, golf courses and arts venues pull buyers in, as do Schreiner University and the Kerrville Folk Festival.

Houses close to the river carry both the appeal and the flood exposure. After the July 2026 flood, that exposure shapes how buyers and insurers view the area, so expect questions about water history on any showing.

sections.h2: The July 2026 flood and your sale
sections.html:
The governor declared Kerr County a disaster area on July 17, 2026, and the city keeps a recovery page with debris collection, damage reporting through the state and a local disaster relief center. If your house was damaged, that history will come up in any sale.

Temporary flood exemption for damaged property

If you missed the window, call Kerr Central Appraisal District and ask whether a late option applies.

sections.h2: What to do about flood or storm damage before selling
sections.html:
Photograph it, then repair it or disclose it, and let the title company know what you claimed through insurance or assistance programs.

  • Keep photos, contractor estimates and receipts for each damaged area.
  • Ask the city whether work needs a permit before a contractor begins.
  • Report damage through the state survey and the local recovery form so officials can track needs.
  • Ask Kerr Central Appraisal District how a temporary exemption affects the value on your account.

A cash buyer can purchase a damaged house as is, which spares you mold remediation and drywall work. Expect the price to reflect the repair scope.

sections.h2: Who appraises property in Kerr County
sections.html:
Kerr Central Appraisal District, at 212 Oak Hollow Drive in Kerrville, appraises all real and business personal property in the county. It has online search, interactive maps, a forms page and an online protest portal.

The entities it serves include Kerr County, the City of Kerrville, Kerrville ISD, Ingram ISD, Center Point ISD, the Upper Guadalupe River Authority and several emergency service districts. Your bill adds several of those together, so read each line. A Hill Country lot outside the city can carry more than one special district line, among them the Upper Guadalupe River Authority and Headwaters Groundwater Conservation District. Your school district appears on your tax statement, and buyers check it first.

sections.h2: Texas tax dates and a Kerrville closing
sections.html:
Value is set on January 1, the lien attaches that day, and bills go out in early October.

  • First half of a split bill: November 30. Second half: June 30.
  • Delinquent from February 1, with penalty and interest.
  • Homestead exemption filings are generally due April 30.
  • Protest deadline is generally May 15, or 30 days after the notice.

A seller closing mid-year normally credits the buyer for the unpaid part of the year at the closing table.

sections.h2: Ways to sell fast in Kerrville
sections.html:
A flood-affected or older house changes which of three routes fits: listing, selling privately or a cash sale.

  • A listing suits a house in good shape on a fair timeline.
  • A for-sale-by-owner sale cuts commission and puts disclosure on you.
  • A cash offer works for as-is houses, absentee owners and estate sales.

In a retirement-heavy Hill Country market, many sales also involve a move to be near family, so a firm closing date is often the deciding factor.

sections.h2: Recording the deed in Kerr County
sections.html: The Kerr County Clerk records deeds for land in the county, and the instrument must be signed and acknowledged before an authorized officer. Texas lists $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each added page, plus other records fees that vary by county. The title company handles filing, so ask for the final charges on your settlement statement.

sections.h2: Transfer on death deeds and land contracts
sections.html:
Texas lets an owner record a transfer on death deed so real property passes without probate, and a Lady Bird deed lets the owner keep selling or mortgaging the house without the beneficiary's consent. Either must be recorded in the county where the property sits, and the transfer on death deed has to be recorded before the owner dies.

A contract for deed is different. Under Property Code chapter 5 the seller keeps title until the buyer finishes paying, and for a residence the buyer has a statutory right to cancel. Seller financing on a Kerrville house is possible, but the rules are strict, so have a Texas attorney draft it.

The Guadalupe River gives Kerrville its parks and its trail, and buyers want to know which parts of town felt the July 2026 flood. The city's recovery page reported Louise Hays Park, Lehmann-Monroe Park, Tranquility Island, Guadalupe Park and the River Trail closed for flood damage, with Knapp Park and Cypress Park reopened.

If your house is on higher ground, say so and show the water history you know. If it took water, a cash buyer will price the repair and a listing buyer will want inspection reports. Accurate answers save time late in the deal. Mention festival weekends, parking and guest space where they apply, and be honest about flood history.

For inherited property, Texas offers a will probate window of four years, a muniment of title when no administration is needed, and a small estate affidavit for estates of $75,000 or less excluding the homestead.

On back taxes, the collector can add up to 20 percent attorney fees under a contract and can pursue a suit. Homestead owners may ask about a delinquent installment plan of up to 36 months where a collector allows it. Call the Kerr County tax office for a payoff figure.

sections.h2: From offer to closing in Kerrville
sections.html:
A normal sale starts with an offer, then an inspection, then a title search and a signing before a notary. In Kerrville, add two flood-related steps: be ready with a clear account of any water history, and have your insurance and assistance claims documented so the title company and buyer see a consistent record.

If the buyer needs a loan, expect an appraisal and lender conditions, which stretch the timeline. A cash buyer can close on your date, and the date matters when you are moving to be near family. Ask for it in writing, along with who pays title charges and recording, so nothing is left to the closing table.

Pull the recorded deed and your latest tax statement from the Kerr County tax office. Add any payoff letter from a lender, photos and receipts for flood damage, permits for repairs, and the account of what insurance covered. If the house is a rental or an inherited property, add the lease or the probate paperwork. A buyer who sees these on day one will often offer faster and with fewer conditions, because there is less to discover later.

faqs.a: The city has thrived since its founding in 1889.

faqs.q: Can I still get the flood property tax exemption in Kerrville?
faqs.a: The filing window ran 105 days from the July 17 declaration. Call Kerr Central Appraisal District and ask whether a late option exists for your property.

faqs.q: What damage level qualified for the temporary exemption?
faqs.a: Kerr CAD said owners with at least 15 percent physical damage could apply, for property in an area the governor declared a disaster.

faqs.q: Where is the Kerr appraisal district office?
Can I sell a flood-damaged house in Kerrville?
faqs.a: Yes, either as is or after you repair it. Gather damage documentation, disclose what you know, and ask the city about permits before any rebuilding.
